lead.hed: USNI: Marines and sailors from San Antonio destroy a suspected narco refueler
lead.insight: USNI News, Monday: Marines and sailors launching from USS San Antonio (LPD-17) interdicted and boarded a vessel suspected of being used as a floating refueling station before Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere destroyed it. The command said it worked with Ecuador. The item is an after-action report on one boarding, not a claim that the Caribbean pipeline is closed.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Derek Cole · DVIDS 9646698 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · USS San Antonio (LPD 17) returns to Naval Station Norfolk, April 28, 2026. Caption must say April file photo, not yesterday’s boarding.
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Navy DVIDS still of USS San Antonio. Same-subject class as the USNI LPD-17 interdiction item — not a brand tile.

political.hed: USNI: Japan’s first Tomahawk destroyer is back in Sasebo
political.insight: USNI News, Monday: JS Chokai (DDG-176) returned Sunday to Sasebo after a year in the United States being outfitted to fire Tomahawk cruise missiles. The ship left Yokosuka for San Diego on Sept. 25, 2025. Tokyo now has a first hull in home waters; fleet-wide inventory and firing certification are still ahead.

political.hed: USNI: Abraham Lincoln transited the Singapore Strait toward Thailand
political.insight: USNI News, Sunday: USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) passed the Singapore Strait Saturday night on the way to a planned port visit in Thailand, according to ship spotters. The carrier and a Japan-based escort were seen transiting toward the South China Sea. The Navy did not post a public itinerary in that item.

political.hed: Defense News: 9/11 tribunal for Khalid Sheikh Mohammed set for June 2028
political.insight: Defense News, Monday, citing Reuters: a U.S. Air Force judge ordered Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and three co-defendants to trial before a military commission in June 2028. The accused 9/11 mastermind has been at Guantanamo for more than two decades. A date on the docket is not a verdict.

tech.hed: Defense News: Pentagon frameworks aim to triple Patriot and quadruple THAAD output
tech.insight: Defense News, Monday: the Pentagon signed framework agreements with Lockheed Martin and General Dynamics to surge interceptor production, including tripling Patriot output and quadrupling THAAD interceptors. Frameworks set targets; they are not finished missiles on the ramp.

tech.hed: Defense News: Sweden orders four French Naval Group frigates
tech.insight: Defense News, Monday: Sweden signed an order for four Naval Group frigates in Stockholm with French President Emmanuel Macron present. The buy is a signed hull order, not a claim the Baltic fleet is already recapitalized.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: the Constitution is not as godless as postliberals say
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Monday: a review argues the American Constitution is not as “godless” as postliberal critics claim, but that the people still have to sustain spiritual capital for it to work. The piece is an argument about founding order, not a court ruling.

culture.hed: WORLD: Colorado’s Catholic preschool funding fight is at the Supreme Court
culture.insight: WORLD, Tuesday morning and Legal Docket: Colorado requires Catholic preschools that take state money to set aside religious standards even as secular providers may tailor enrollment. WORLD frames it as a First Amendment conflict now headed to the Court. Oral argument is still ahead.
